prompt.brief: Design a multimodal AI assistant that accepts text, images, audio, and video, extracts and fuses relevant representations, answers or generates content, and takes authorized actions with safe fallbacks.
successSignals: Separate original media, extracted transcripts and embeddings, conversation state, model policy, tool permissions, and outputs.
Use modality-specific preprocessing and bounded fusion context, with asynchronous video/audio work and streaming text responses.
Apply input, retrieval, action, and output safety controls; require confirmation for consequential or irreversible actions.
Explain modality failure, latency budgets, privacy, prompt injection, media retention, and cost-aware model routing.

functional: Upload or stream modalities, transcribe and analyze media, answer questions, generate responses, and invoke authorized tools.
Show citations or media evidence, partial progress, confidence, safety decisions, tool results, and conversation history.
Support cancellation, media deletion, tenant isolation, consent, feedback, export, and model/version traceability.
nonFunctional: Target p95 text time to first token below one second while longer audio and video analysis reports progress asynchronously.
Handle 50,000 concurrent sessions with modality-specific queues and per-tenant media and token quotas.
Make uploads, turns, tool calls, moderation, and usage accounting idempotent and auditable.
Fall back to text-only or a smaller model when a modality encoder, GPU pool, or external tool is unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Support 50,000 concurrent sessions, 10,000 turns per second, and large audio/video uploads with varied durations.
Partition by tenant, conversation, modality, and model; isolate long media jobs and high-volume assistants.
Retain encrypted source media, consent, safety decisions, transcripts, and tool audit while bounding active context.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Multimodal AI assistant commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Multimodal AI assistant writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Multimodal AI assistant version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Multimodal AI assistant by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Multimodal AI assistant work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Multimodal AI assistant projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Multimodal AI assistant projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Multimodal AI assistant records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Multimodal AI assistant latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
